purpose: Test whether a newly trained permutation-equivariant C4-free edge policy can outperform an information-matched endpoint scorer and the strong nonlearned polarity baselines on unseen sizes.
model: Original EdgePolicy with 64 hidden units and 3 message-passing layers (GNN) or 0 (endpoint), retrained from scratch on new C4-specific features and action mask.
optimizer: AdamW 3e-4, weight decay 1e-4, cross-entropy on selected elite-prefix actions, gradient norm clip 1.0; equal settings and budgets for both families.
checkpoint_selection: Best n20 validation mean edges among eight fixed events, earliest event wins exact ties.
evaluation: Five fresh sizes per model/seed with independent per-episode torch RNG, 100 episodes per cell. Save every final graph; independently verify C4-freeness and maximality. n20 is the training size; 24/30/35/40 are extrapolations.
comparison: Exploratory: report seed-level GNN versus endpoint means and compare both to the separately frozen nonlearned polarity/polarity_swap200 pilot at the same sizes. Practical solver success requires exceeding the polarity baseline at n35 and n40, while published exact values remain the reference. No inferential superiority claim from three training seeds.
budget: Each run has 5,120 terminal training rollouts, 320 optimizer updates, 800 validation episodes; total construction actions depend on policy trajectories. Training and inference wall time are recorded but methods are not equal-time competitors.
limits: Neural experiment was chosen after seeing the nonneural pilot, so it is exploratory. The published exact table is not used for training reward, model selection, or action ranking. This first fixed-budget CEM configuration is not an equal-tuning or equal-capacity architecture test. The small seed count and inspected target sizes preclude a definitive generalization claim.
